messages:
sara_p: devs, noticed a sharp p99 increase on eu1 A10 cluster right after the 202->main merge, started ~08:12UTC. p50 fine, p99 up ~2.2x. Can someone take a look? :eyes:
cheng: on it. any rollout blockers reported by deploy-bot?
deploy-bot: Deploy main@202 finished at 08:07UTC to eu1-a10 pool, canary 3/3 healthy.
mike_w: throwing a profiler on a victim host now, will attach traces. suspicious this is kernel selector change from the merge.
amelia: queueing traces and kvcache metrics. I seeKV eviction spikes correlated with the p99 in prometheus, starting 08:12.
sara_p: I also see more `kernel_fallback` events in logs around the same time. Maybe selector is falling back to generic kernel for certain seq len distributions?
cheng: running a diff of kernel selection table between main@201 and main@202. early result: a new rule for L4 batching heuristics was added that increases batch window for small seqs when throughput > 80%. Could interact badly with A10 scheduling.
mike_w: profiler output from a slow request (sanitized):
```
PROFILE: host=a10-27
cpu idle: 12%
kernel_selected: generic-attn-v2
latency: 310ms (p99)
kv_cache: miss -> full-evict cycle at 08:12:19
network qlen spikes: 220 -> 900
```
amelia: KV cache TTL and prefetch look normal, but eviction rate high. I'm seeing repeated full-page invalidations from kvcache due to key fragmentation after batching heuristic changed.
sara_p: could noisy neighbor NIC egress plus kernel fallback cause this? we've seen NIC queueing push RT to KV eviction before.
mike_w: ran `ss -tnp` during the event, saw many retransmits on the RDMA path. suspect a transient egress bandwidth contention.
cheng: ordering hypothesis: new batching heuristic increases batch window -> larger batches -> higher transient NIC egress bursts -> packet loss -> retransmits -> kernel selector observes stalls -> falls back to slower generic-attn kernel -> longer KV iterations -> mem pressure -> kvcache evictions -> p99 spike.
amelia: nice causal chain. can we validate by forcing the old kernel rule? I can patch the selector config and spin a 2-host canary.
sara_p: +1 do it. also open a CI perf job to reproduce under controlled noisy-egress.
ops-bot: CI perf job queued: perf/job/selector-a10-noisy-egress-199900 queued. ETA ~20m.
mike_w: quick hotfix: revert the batching-window change in a local canary, after revert the p99 dropped back to baseline within 3 minutes. We should consider revert on main if canary confirms.
cheng: bisect plan: 1) reproduce in perf CI with synthetic egress noise, 2) test selector config revert in canary, 3) if passes, ship revert PR and block rollout.
amelia: I've captured the kselector logs for the time window and put them in /tmp/trace-199900.tar.gz on the infra-share. Key line: `selector: rule=small_seq_batch widen_ms=12 -> applied to queue a10-27` repeated.
sara_p: thanks. assign owners: cheng for bisect + revert PR, amelia for KV eviction profiling + mitigations, mike for networking traces and documenting noisy neighbor mitigation patterns. I'll own the revert if green.
mike_w: note: H100 clusters not impacted in same way, likely because kernel choice and NIC offload differ; L4 microkernel uses different RDMA codepath.
cheng: added a rollback label to main rollout. If CI perf job fails we hold.
ops-bot: CI perf job perf/job/selector-a10-noisy-egress-199900 finished: regression reproduced (p99 +210%). Artifacts: link://ci/199900.
sara_p: holding rollout. I'll open PR to revert the batching-window change and include the canary results.
amelia: also prototyping a KV prefetch guard to reduce full evicts under transient NIC loss. won't be ready for immediate revert but good medium-term fix.
mike_w: +:thumbsup: will add network egress shaping docs for on-host scheduler to avoid large bursts.
sara_p: thanks team. next update after canary revert results or CI confirms. :eyes:
